newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suspected World War Two landmine kills Egyptian.
newsitem.headline: Suspected World War Two landmine kills Egyptian.

text.p: An Egyptian was killed and another injured on Tuesday when they stepped on a land mine in a quarry near the northern Red Sea town of Suez, security sources said.
Egypt was the scene of several Allied and Axis battles in World War Two, during which both sides planted millions of mines.
The sources said Ra'fat Shabana Mohammed, 29, died and his colleague Hammada Mostafa Allam, 23, was hurt when the mine exploded while they were working at the quarry.

The Cairo government has in the past asked World War Two foes Britain and Germany to help it find and remove about 23 million land mines the two countries planted in the Egyptian desert during their battle for control over North Africa.

Government officials say Egypt is the country with the highest number of land mines in the world. They say the mines are distributed in the western desert and the Sinai peninsula over an area of about 288,000 hectares (710,000 acres).
